title: Pages
lead: Create independent working drafts, publish reviewed snapshots and compose layouts from typed public data.

sections.title: Create and edit
body: Create a page from a generic model; duplication is a separate action. The immutable page ID remains stable when a published URL changes.

Use the shared visual/code editor and media picker. Save draft preserves the live page; publish, unpublish and schedule are explicit actions. SEO and social overrides inherit editorial/global defaults.

sections.title: Add components
body: Use Insert component to choose a registered plugin service and a template-supported format. The generated marker is inserted in a content section. Block markers must occupy their own paragraph.
Legacy Slides markers and typed slide blocks remain supported. Components show only data that the provider permits publicly.

sections.title: Publish and recover
body: Ordinary pages can be drafts or published. Homepage and 404 are protected published pages. Preview requires an authenticated session.
Trash preserves removable pages in revision history. Restore only from a listed revision; concurrent edits are rejected rather than overwritten.

sections.title: Shared HTML and public page data
body: The optional HTML / Mustache panel in a page editor uses the same core renderer as Homepage. Enabling it replaces the structured body view while preserving the page metadata and original structured JSON. Disable it to return to that original structure. Bind multiple public services, then write semantic HTML and loops manually. pages:list(limit:1–12) supplies items with title, text, href and image, excluding reserved home/404 pages, drafts and deleted pages.

Pages is a document source for Homepage: choose a published page by slug. The source adapter supplies its common semantic content (title, summary, facts and sections) or its authored HTML; it does not duplicate the native template frame or all template-specific extras. Editing the source updates the next request. A missing source never exposes a draft.

sections.title: Author HTML with shared Mustache data
body: Use the shared HTML/Mustache editor to write manual sections, choose plugin services, add typed bindings and insert the documented loops. Metadata is edited in separate fields and saved with the body. Public data is resolved at render time.

Pages keeps native content behind an optional markup override. Blog keeps existing typed blocks unless HTML mode is explicitly selected; only the selected mode is saved. A mode switch does not convert old blocks automatically. See docs/authoring-customizations.md for the complete workflow.

sections.title: Shared visual editor
body: HTML/Mustache content opens in the shared core visual editor. Use Visual for static content, Code for advanced structure and protected dynamic blocks, and Preview for an isolated template-CSS view. Opening or switching modes does not rewrite the original source.

Select content before applying formatting, links or images. Enter creates another paragraph. Bindings discover the enabled plugins; Insert block appends a validated Mustache snippet. Variables, loops, Forms and template fragments keep their existing server-side contracts.

CSS, JavaScript and PHP are separate code-authoring profiles available to plugin developers. PHP is never executed or published by this editor. Global supplemental CSS/JavaScript retain their own draft, validation, history and explicit publishing workflow.

sections.title: Shared media and data
body: Global Settings owns public/private repository roots; Images owns uploads. Public page editors can select only public media.

Pages records, details, children and breadcrumbs services deliver typed data without HTML. Receiver layouts own escaped Mustache variables and loops. Recovering a deleted page or revision produces a draft.
